1  AWAR D 1.
This is claim petition filed u/s 166 and 140 M.V. Act for claim of compensation regarding death of deceased Rajesh.
As per the facts on 07.10.2014 at about 21.15 hours deceased Rajesh was traveling as a pillion rider on a motorcycle and was coming toward Delhi from Sikandarabad with his friend Sandeep Kumar.

When they reached near Village Khera Dharmpura, G.T. road, Greater Noida, a truck bearing registration no.UP- 14B-9570 came in very high speed and hit the motorcycle of the deceased due to which both riders of the motorcycle including deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
The injured were immediately taken to the District Hospital, Noida, for his medical treatment and during the treatment deceased succumbed to accidental injuries.

In respect of accident in question, FIR No.195/2014 (Crime No.343/2014) was registered in PS Badalpur,
District Gautam Budh Nagar, for offence under Section 279, 338, 304A, 427 IPC.
As per police report offending vehicle i.e. truck no.UP- 14B-9570 was being driven by respondent no.1 and owned by respondent no.2.
Offending vehicle was found to be insured with New India Insurance Company Ltd. (respondent no.3).
During the investigation post mortem of the deceased was got conducted.

2. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed WS to the claim petition taking an objection that respondent no.1 has been falsely implicated in the accident MACT No.1049/2016 Page 2 case and that no accident has been caused by respondent no.1.
As such the present claim petition is without any cause of action against respondent no.1 and 2.
It is stated that even otherwise the vehicle in question no. UP 14B 9570 was duly insured.
Other contents of claim petition have been denied.

3. Respondent no.3/New India Assurance Company Limited filed the WS taking the objection that the alleged occurrence of accident having taken place by the offending vehicle as claimed has not been substantiated by any FIR, charge sheet, MLC, post mortem report and other documents.
As such the accident as well as causing of same by respondent no.1 by rash and negligent driving has been denied.

Further objection was taken that this Tribunal has no territorial jurisdiction to entertain the claim petition as accident took place within the jurisdiction of PS Badalpur (Dadri),
District Gautam Budh Nagar, UP and actual address of the victim/petitioners are also of PS Kotwali,
District Ghaziabad, UP.
Contents of claim petition have been denied.
It is further stated that negligence on the part of the driver of motorcycle no. UP 14CF 5989 can also be not ruled out in the facts of the present case.
Moreover driver of the said motorcycle was not holding effective and valid DL.

It is further pleaded that respondent no.3/ insurance can indemnify the amount of compensation if the terms of the insurance policy have not been violated, whereas in this case terms and conditions of insurance policy have been violated as the offending vehicle UP 14B 9570 was not having valid and effective fitness certificate and thus was not in a perfect road worthy condition.

4. On the basis of pleadings of parties, ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal framed following issues on 07.05.2015 :
1)Whether Sh.Rajesh suffered fatal injuries in the accident occurred MACT No.1049/2016 Page 3 on 07.10.2014 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No.
UP- 14B-9570 (Truck) being driven by respondent No.1?
(OPP) (2)Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?

2 OPP (3)Relief.
5.
By order dated 28.08.2015 ld.
Predecessor of this Court awarded interim amount of compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 9% from date of filing of petition till realization.
Rs.53,440/- was given to petitioner by way of cheque no.526837 of Corporation Bank as reflected in order dated 09.10.2015.
6. It is matter of record that issues in this claim petition were framed on 07.05.2015 and thereafter matter was fixed for recording P.E.
Matter remained pending for recording PE uptill 27.10.2022 when ld. counsel for petitioner closed PE.
Thus petitioners took about seven years to complete their evidence.
7. In order to substantiate its case petitioner examined two witnesses i.e. PW1 is Smt.Sunita wife of deceased, PW2 is Yogeshwar son of Gyan Chand who is stated to be an eye witness of the accident.
8. On behalf of respondent no.1 and 2, respondent no.1 Ram Roop/ driver has appeared in the witness box as R1W1.
Respondent no.3/ insurance has also examined one witness i.e. R3W1 Gulam Rabbani, from ARTO District Fatehpur, UP.
9. I have heard Sh.Ajay Kumar Gautam, ld. Counsel for petitioner, Sh. Rajesh Goel, ld. Counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
I have also gone through synopsis/break up of claim on behalf of petitioners as well as written submissions.
Issue No.1 MACT No.1049/2016 Page 4 10.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.

sentences.text: In the facts of the present case PW1 Smt.Sunita in her deposition has testified that her husband met with a road side accident on 07.10.2014 near village Kheda, G.T. Road, Greater Noida with truck no. UP 14B 9570.
PW1 was obviously not an eye witness.

PW1 however in her evidence proved certified copy of criminal record as Ex.PW1/D.
12.

Petitioner examined PW2 Yogeshwar as an eye witness who deposed that on 07.10.2014, he was standing opposite Sariya Godown, near Village Khera, Dharampur City Road, Greater Noida, at Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
3 about 09.15 p.m. all of sudden truck bearing registration no.UP 14B 9570 came from Lal Kual side and was going towards Dadri in a very high speed and being driven in a rash and negligent manner hit the motorcyclist, due to impact both the motorcyclist fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
PW2 stated that police officials of local police station came at the spot and took the injured/deceased to district hospital Sector 30.

PW2 states that MACT No.1049/2016 Page 5 accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
13.

Driver of offending vehicle/respondent no.1 Ram Roop has appeared as R1W1 and deposed in his affidavit that no accident has been caused by him as alleged and vehicle in question has been falsely implicated in FIR No.195/2014.

Counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company challenged the testimony of PW2 and submitted that evidence of PW2 does not establish the rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle, even by preponderance of probabilities.

Ld. Counsel for R3 submits that in the cross-examination of PW2 it has come that there is no documentary evidence of PW2 being present at the time of accident and that his statement was neither recorded by local police nor before ld.
MM.
As such there is a serious doubt if PW2 was actually eye witness to the accident or not.
Consequently ld. Counsel submits that factum of accident having taken place by rash and negligent driving of R1 could not be proved.
In the absence of same respondent no.3/insurance company cannot be held liable for compensation.
15. Having considered the submissions and taking note of evidence and other material on judicial record, as noted above in an inquiry before MAC Tribunal,
the standard of proof for proving accident having taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle is not the same as is required in a criminal or in civil case.

In the present case no doubt there are certain suspicious circumstances creeping in the cross- examination of PW2 such as that whether his statement was recorded during the investigation of the criminal case by the IO of the FIR No.195/2014.
It further came in the cross-examination of PW2 that he never called the police after the accident nor he accompanied with the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 6 injured of the accident/victim to hospital.

However this Tribunal finds that these circumstances though create certain doubts as to the veracity of evidence of PW2 but that fact in itself is not sufficient to completely discard the evidence of PW2 for proof of rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 causing the accident in which deceased Rajesh expired.

Moreover even if for the time being evidence of PW2 is ignored, still this Tribunal finds sufficient material available on the record proving the factum of accident, rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
16.
The facts that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.

Reference may be given to judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case titled as Shabina v.
Satvir & Ors. MAC. APP. 980/17 dated 24.01.2020, wherein it has been observed that in so far as FIR has been registered, criminal case has been initiated against driver of offending vehicle and vehicle was seized, the requirement of proving the preponderance of probability of accident having been caused by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle has been established.

On perusal of the award of the Tribunal, it becomes clear that the wife of the deceased had produced (i) certified copy of the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 7 criminal record of criminal case in FIR No. 955/2004, pertaining to involvement of the offending vehicle,
(ii) Criminal record showing completion of investigation of police and issue of charge sheet under Section 279/304-A IPC against the driver, (iii) certified copy of FIR,
wherein criminal case against the driver was lodged; and (iv) recovery memo and mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle and vehicle of the deceased.
These documents are sufficient proofs to reach the conclusion that the driver was negligent.
Proceedings under Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

Hence,
this contention of the counsel of the appellant also falls face down.
There is ample evidence on record to prove negligence on the part of driver."
17. Besides above, post mortem report, the certified copy of which is part of criminal case record Ex.PW1/D, which show that deceased died due to RTA (road traffic accident).

As per post mortem report deceased suffered abrasion/contusion at right side of forehead, contusion around left eye,
multiple abrasions all over face, abrasion over left side of chest, abrasion at right shoulder, multiple abrasions over right wrist and hand, abrasions over hand, knee and back which according to the post mortem doctor were ante mortem and accidental injuries causing the death of the deceased.
18.

Beside this there is report u/s 173 Cr.PC in FIR No.195/2014 (Crime case no.343/2014) of PS Badalpur (Dadri), Gautam Budh Nagar wherein respondent no.1 being the driver of the offending vehicle no. UP 14B 9570 was charge sheeted and prosecuted in the criminal court.

There is a certified copy of site plan of the place of accident prepared during investigation of that case as well as the mechanical inspection report of MACT No.1049/2016 Page 8 motorcycle no.UP 14CF 5989.
Moreover in the cross-examination of driver R1W1 it came that he was arrested by the police in FIR No.195/2014 of PS Badalpur and criminal case regarding the accident in question is pending against him in Gautam Budh Nagar.

All these material coupled with the evidence of PW2, in the opinion of this Tribunal are sufficient to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Rajesh.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.

Issue No.2 Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
5 19.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners i.e. wife, children and parents of deceased are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

20. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Rajesh.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121

Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench MACT No.1049/2016 Page 9 of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi &
Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"18.
It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

6 19.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 10 dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
22.

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased :
23.
PW1 Sunita Sharma wife of deceased in her affidavit has deposed that her husband was aged 40 years on the day of accident.
PW1 MACT No.1049/2016 Page 11
was not cross-
examined on this aspect.
This fact is not much of any dispute either in pleadings or in evidence.

Even otherwise PW1 proved the ration card as Ex.PW1/C,
police documents including Post mortem report coupled with her testimony which established that deceased at the time of his death was 40 years of age.

7
Assessment of Income of deceased :

24. Petitioner (PW1) in her deposition stated that her deceased husband was having good physique and was working in a private company as boiler operator with Park Plaza Hotel Delhi and drawing Rs.20,000/- per month.

25. Ld. counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company has submitted that no evidence has been led by petitioner in support of her claim that deceased used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month and was working as boiler operator in a private company.
He further submitted that even petitioner has not brought any evidence on record to show that deceased was resident of Delhi.

26. Having taken into consideration the evidence of PW1 on record, PW1 though claims that her husband was earning Rs.20,000/- per month at the time of accident and was working as boiler operator in Park Plaza Hotel, Delhi.
But PW1 in cross-examination admits that she has no documentary proof regarding occupation and income of her deceased husband or his employment proof.

PW1 further stated that deceased had taken a vocational training with National Council for Vocational Training, under Ministry of Labour, Government of India (from Industrial Training Institute) and took apprentice and took provisional apprentice certificate which is Ex.PW1/E.

sentences.text: Thus in the absence of any evidence of proof of employment, income of deceased but taking into consideration the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 12 apprentice certificate Ex.PW1/E of deceased, this Tribunal finds that income of the deceased would be considered to be at the parity with minimum wages for semi-skilled labour as prevalent in the State of U.P. as accident took place in UP.
As per evidence of PW1 deceased was living in Ghaziabad, UP.
Thus the income of the deceased found to be Rs.271.43 per day i.e. Rs.8,142.90/- per month.

Application of Multiplier:
27.
As held above, deceased was 40 years of age at the time of accident.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
In Para 21 of the judgment, the guidelines for the multiplier were laid down in accordance with age are as under:

MULTIPLIER AGE GROUP OF DECEASED  M-18 Age group between 15 to 20 & 21  to 25 years)
 M-17 Age group between 26 to 30 yrs  M-16 Age group between 31 to 35 yrs  M-15 Age group between 36 to 40 yrs  M-14 Age group between 41 to 45 yrs  M-13 Age group between 46 to 50 yrs  M-11 Age group between 51 to 55 yrs  M-9 Age group between 56 to 60 yrs Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
8  M-7
Age group between 61 to 65 yrs
M-5 Age group between 66 and above 28.
In view of the above, multiplier of 15 has to be applied against 40 years of age of the deceased to determine the compensation.

Future Prospects:
MACT No.1049/2016 Page 13 29.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra).

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

The established income means the income minus the tax component."
30.
The deceased can be considered a temporary employee.
In view of the above said judgment, an addition of 30% of the income of deceased (aged 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

Deduction towards Personal Living Expenses:
31.
After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
MACT No.1049/2016 Page 14  Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3 Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
9  Where the number of dependent family 1/4th  members is 4 to 6  Where the number of dependent family 1/5th  members exceeds 6 (six)
32.

sentences.text: Instant claim petition has been filed by two petitioners i.e. parents of deceased.
Since, the deceased was survived by two dependents, one-fourth of the income of the deceased is to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
33.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-, 18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

INTEREST ON AWARD 36.
Interest in this case is awarded @ 6% per annum on account of the fact that predominantly delay in this matter has been caused by petitioners for not completing PE for long period of time.
LIABILITY 37.
Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
Accident in question has taken place on MACT No.1049/2016 Page 16 07.10.2014 from offending vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration no.UP 14B 9570 which was being driven by respondent no.1 Ram Roop.

Driver Ram Roop has appeared in the witness box as R1W1 and stated in his affidavit that at the time of accident the truck in question was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company and that he was having a valid DL No.UP7120080102299 issued on 07.08.2008 by RTO of Fatehpur, UP, which was valid upto 08.12.2025.
R1W1 further deposed that having heavy licence for running transport vehicle he got first transport licence no. R10437/F/0/09 which was renewed from time to time.

The copy of the licence is Ex.R1W1/1.
38.

Insurance company/respondent no.3 on the other hand examined R3W1 Gulam Rabbani from ARTO District Fatehpur who brought the original record regarding DL issued by ARTO Fatehpur no.R10437/F issued in the name of Ram Roop s/o Ramu Shiromani which was issue don 07.08.2008 and was valid for 06.08.2028, for driving non transport four wheelers and two wheelers.

R3W1 further testifies that DL was endorsed for driving transport vehicle w.e.f. 19.11.2009 to 08.11.2012 and was renewed for driving transport vehicle on 10.10.2014 and remained valid till 09.10.2017.
There was a gap between 18.11.2012 to 10.10.2014 for which period driver was not authorized to drive transport vehicles.
Relevant page of the register is Ex.R3W1/1.

Computerized certified copy of licencing authority Fatehpur is Ex.R3W1/2.
39.
It is argued by ld.
Counsel for insurance company
that from the evidence of PW R3W1, it is established that driver was not having a valid DL for driving transport vehicle i.e. truck.
As such there was a clear violation of terms of the insurance policy due to which R3 is not liable for the amount of compensation.
MACT No.1049/2016 Page 17 40

. Having considered evidence of R3W1, DL Ex.R3W1/1 and Ex.R3W1/2, admittedly the DL no.
R10437/F/0/08 of respondent no.1 was valid for non transport (LMV, MCWG) from 07.08.2008 to 06.08.2028, four wheelers and two wheelers.

Said DL was valid for transport vehicles from Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
11 09.12.2020 to 08.12.2025.
Said DL was endorsed for driving transport vehicle w.e.f. 19.11.2009 to 08.11.2012 and was renewed for driving transport vehicle on 10.10.2014 and remained valid till 09.10.2017.

There was a gap between 18.11.2012 to 10.10.2014.
41.

Thus, from examining the report Ex.R3W1/2 as well as the extract of driving licence annexed therewith it is evident that DL was valid for LMV, four wheeler non transport but was not valid for transport purposes from 18.11.2012 to 10.10.2014.
Accident in question took place on 07.10.2014.

Even if accident has been caused by the truck i.e. offending vehicle being driven by R1, still R1 was having valid non transport LMV DL.
42.

sentences.text: The above said judgment of Apex Court has been referred to Constitutional Bench.

In the meantime recently Apex Court in M/s Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Rambha Devi and Ors. (Civil Appeal No.841/2018), while noting that the judgment of Mukund Devangan is under consideration before MACT No.1049/2016 Page 18 Constitutional Bench, matter was referred to Government for evaluation to embark upon interpretative exercise.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
11.
PW1 was obviously not an eye witness.
the standard of proof for proving accident having taken place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle is not the same as is required in a criminal or in civil case.
In the present case no doubt there are certain suspicious circumstances creeping in the cross- examination of PW2 such as that whether his statement was recorded during the investigation of the criminal case by the IO of the FIR No.195/2014.
Moreover even if for the time being evidence of PW2 is ignored, still this Tribunal finds sufficient material available on the record proving the factum of accident, rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1.
16.
The facts that FIR has been registered and criminal proceedings have been initiated against the respondent no.1 by the police, are sufficient proof to conclude that respondent no.1 was negligent.
In the aforesaid case, Hon'ble Delhi High Court referred to the judgment titled as National Insurance Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/

All these material coupled with the evidence of PW2, in the opinion of this Tribunal are sufficient to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that has resulted into fatal injuries to deceased Rajesh.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners i.e. wife, children and parents of deceased are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
20. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 21.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 10 dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Thus in the absence of any evidence of proof of employment, income of deceased but taking into consideration the MACT No.1049/2016 Page 12 apprentice certificate Ex.PW1/E of deceased, this Tribunal finds that income of the deceased would be considered to be at the parity with minimum wages for semi-skilled labour as prevalent in the State of U.P. as accident took place in UP.
Thus the income of the deceased found to be Rs.271.43 per day i.e. Rs.8,142.90/- per month.
An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.
Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65, in para 30, laid down the necessary deductions towards personal living and expenses of deceased as under :
MACT No.1049/2016 Page 14  Deductions out of earning of the Number of  deceased dependents  Where dependent is 1 Half  Where the number of dependent family 1/3rd  members is 2 to 3 Sunita vs Ram Roop on 18 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185540131/
